_about: PaedScale external validation, extension set (PROTOCOL.md Amendment 19). Engine inputs from FDA label snapshots (paths relative to backend/benchmark/); every quote is checked by tests/test_external_extension.py. Harness only: never read by the product path.

cefazolin.label: labels/cefazolin.json

fe.quote: In the first 6 hours approximately 60% of the drug is excreted in the urine and this increases to 70% to 80% within 24 hours

cefazolin.notes: Label: 'excreted unchanged in the urine'. Longest collection (24 h), range midpoint.

digoxin.label: labels/digoxin.json

fe.quote: Following intravenous administration to healthy volunteers, 50-70% of a digoxin dose is excreted unchanged in the urine

digoxin.notes: Non-renal fraction: label says metabolism is not CYP-dependent, so it stays unattributed.

fentanyl.label: labels/fentanyl.json

fe.quote: mostly as metabolites with less than 10% representing the unchanged drug

fentanyl.enzyme_evidence: literature: fentanyl metabolism by hepatic CYP3A4 (Labroo et al., Drug Metab Dispos 1997;25:1072-80, PMID 9311623)
fentanyl.notes: fe stated only as an upper bound (<10%); scored at the midpoint of [0, 10%].

alfentanil.reason: No openFDA label has openfda.generic_name alfentanil with an intravenous route, so the selection rule returns no label and E3 cannot be assessed.

sufentanil.label: external/extension/labels/sufentanil.json

fe.quote: only 2% of the dose is eliminated as unchanged drug

sufentanil.enzyme_evidence: literature: CYP3A4 N-dealkylation of fentanyl and sufentanil (Tateishi et al., Anesth Analg 1996;82:167-72, PMID 8712396)

fe.quote: 91.3 ± 5.0% (n = 4) of intravenously administered ganciclovir was recovered unmetabolized in the urine

cefotaxime.label: external/extension/labels/cefotaxime.json

fe.quote: Approximately 20-36% of an intravenously administered dose of 14 C-cefotaxime is excreted by the kidney as unchanged cefotaxime

cefotaxime.notes: Non-renal fraction (desacetylation) is not CYP3A4 or UGT2B7, so it stays unattributed.

levofloxacin.label: external/extension/labels/levofloxacin.json

fe.quote: approximately 87% of an administered dose was recovered as unchanged drug in urine within 48 hours

levofloxacin.notes: The label's only quantitative fe follows oral dosing.

milrinone.label: external/extension/labels/milrinone.json

fe.quote: The major urinary excretions of orally administered milrinone in man are milrinone (83%) and its 0-glucuronide metabolite (12%)

milrinone.notes: The label's only quantitative fe follows oral dosing.

ceftriaxone.label: external/extension/labels/ceftriaxone.json

fe.quote: Thirty-three percent to 67% of a ceftriaxone dose was excreted in the urine as unchanged drug and the remainder was secreted in the bile

ceftriaxone.notes: Non-renal fraction is biliary, not enzymatic, so it stays unattributed.

linezolid.label: external/extension/labels/linezolid.json
linezolid.reason: The label states that clearance is nonlinear with dose.
linezolid.quote: A small degree of nonlinearity in clearance was observed with increasing doses of linezolid

metronidazole.label: external/extension/labels/metronidazole.json

fe.quote: unchanged metronidazole accounting for approximately 20% of the total
fe.quote_2: The major route of elimination of metronidazole and its metabolites is via the urine (60 to 80% of the dose)

metronidazole.notes: Unchanged drug is about 20% of urinary recovery, which is 60 to 80% of the dose (quote_2): fe = 0.20 × 0.70. Oxidation and glucuronidation are not attributed to a curve.
